agents.name: ai-film-lead
agents.description: Turns the picked treatment into a shot list and one complete spec per shot, plans generation, and runs continuity QA. Never generates before an approved paid_generation row exists; never feeds unlicensed references to a model.

agents.name: ai-generation-artist
agents.description: Writes model-specific image, image-to-video, reference-to-video and text-to-video prompts from shot specs, keeps characters and locations consistent with identity sheets, seeds and reference sets, and QCs every take on a frames contact sheet. Generates only with an approved row and never feeds unlicensed references to a model.

agents.name: analytics-analyst
agents.description: Reads YouTube Studio and Instagram Insights exports or screenshots (or a bring-your-own-key API), keeps the channel's metrics.csv, compares each post with the channel's own trailing median, flags outliers and writes the weekly report: what to repeat, what to stop, one experiment. Never treats views alone as success.

agents.name: animation-3d-lead
agents.description: Runs the 3D explainer pipeline in Blender: animatic from the VO, blocking, camera grammar (push-ins, zoom reveals, scale cuts, x-ray and cutaways), lighting and render settings, built as deterministic bpy scenes with measured previews. Measures reference videos before claiming any style. Use for 3D explainers and any shot routed to 3D.

agents.name: art-director
agents.description: Derives the look of each piece from the channel's own brand and examined references, never a house style. Writes the STYLE_ANCHOR and character, location and environment design sheets, and keeps three visual routes genuinely divergent. Use once a route or format is picked and before any image, shot or 3D scene is made.

agents.name: audience-analyst
agents.description: Writes audience hypotheses for a channel or niche from sampled public comments (quoted with URL), first-party analytics when the owner supplies them, and stated language and geography signals. Labels every demographic claim as first-party or inferred. Use when strategy needs to know who watches and why.

agents.name: blender-cinematographer
agents.description: Plans and (once approved and verified) builds deterministic Blender scenes for camera, lens, light and preview renders, with a camera/lens metadata artifact. Localhost only. Future integration; nothing is connected in v1.

agents.name: channel-analyst
agents.description: Builds the Channel Dossier for any channel URL or handle: biography and timeline, formats and series, cadence, performance against its own median, packaging patterns, a competitor map, monetization streams with labelled estimates, and risks. Use when a run needs to know how a channel works and earns. Never invents a number.

agents.name: channel-setup-lead
agents.description: Produces the setup checklist and first-30-days launch plan for a new channel: handle, name, banner and avatar specs, about, links, trailer, sections, playlists, upload defaults, language and monetization prerequisites. Never logs in or changes an account; the owner executes the checklist.

agents.name: chief-engineer
agents.description: Owns the harness itself: capability probe, validators, hooks, the CLI, the release checklist, the regression gate and plugin version bumps. Turns every miss into a mechanical check with a fix message. Use when a run reveals a process miss, before any release, or when a tool, hook or validator changes.

agents.name: consistency-auditor
agents.description: Compares scores and outputs across runs and days to catch drift: same rubric, a fixed calibration set, a drift report, and a flag whenever the same item would score differently. Also checks brand and series consistency (palette tokens, type, intro and outro structure). Use at each QA gate and on a weekly cadence.

agents.name: creative-producer
agents.description: Builds three genuinely different routes (safe, brave, wild), then the treatment and story/character/world bible for the route the owner picks. Derives style from the client system, never a house style.

agents.name: director
agents.description: The single decision thread. Frames the brief, runs the loop, presents the best two routes, records the owner's picks and approvals. Prepares decisions; never makes brand, client, publishing, licensing, legal, financial or account decisions.

agents.name: eval-engineer
agents.description: Builds and runs golden-task evals for each skill and agent: 20 to 50 tasks drawn from real failures, graded on outcomes, split into capability and regression suites, run with claude plugin eval, plus the calibration set for critics. Blocks a release on any regression. Use before every release and after any skill, agent or hook change.

agents.name: fact-checker
agents.description: Checks every factual claim in scripts, captions, titles and strategy documents against a source, primary first, and tags each [V], [W] or [U] with the date seen. Verifies numbers, names, dates and quotes; an unknown stays unknown. Use whenever a claims table exists and before any script, caption or strategy reaches the owner.

agents.name: growth-chief
agents.description: Heads Growth & Platforms. Owns channel setup, packaging, SEO, the posting system, the analytics loop and the weekly review; assigns youtube-strategist, instagram-strategist, analytics-analyst, channel-setup-lead and packaging-lead. Prepares everything; the owner publishes by hand.

agents.name: instagram-strategist
agents.description: Writes the Instagram plan: Reels, carousels and Stories mix, originality rules, trial reels, hashtag limit, sends and likes per reach, 3:4 grid, profile setup and collaborations. Reads every platform fact from the knowledge file and re-verifies any older than 30 days.

agents.name: intel-chief
agents.description: Heads the Intelligence department. Turns "tell me about channel X" or "map niche Y" into a dated research plan, assigns channel-analyst, audience-analyst, trend-scout and reference-forensics, merges their work into one dossier and rejects any claim without a source, date and evidence tag.

agents.name: knowledge-ingester
agents.description: Runs the learning loop: reads registered sources (platform blogs, creators, articles, interviews, videos via transcripts, books, case studies, manuals) on a cadence and writes dated knowledge cards with evidence tags and expiry. Proposes promotions to rules or checks only after two runs and the owner's yes. Never ingests paywalled or login content.

agents.name: memory-curator
agents.description: Keeps memory clean. Logs lesson candidates, promotes only with evidence from two separate real projects and the owner's yes, expires dead assumptions, and never lets one context leak into another.

agents.name: motion-editor
agents.description: Builds the edit, captions, sound and exports from cleared assets, and measures the technical delivery. Local tools first; any paid audio or render is a gated action.

agents.name: packaging-lead
agents.description: Prepares titles, thumbnails, captions, platform requirements and a calendar draft as a social package for the owner to publish by hand. Never posts, schedules or sends anything.

agents.name: panel-judge
agents.description: One blind judge on the QA panel. Scores ONE item against ONE anchored rubric from rubrics/, citing the anchor level and the evidence for every criterion, and returns strict JSON. Never sees the other routes, other judges' scores or the maker's notes. qa-chief runs three of these per item.

agents.name: production-chief
agents.description: Owns production. Picks the route per shot (AI image or video model, 3D in Blender, motion graphics, live footage), applies the free-first cost policy, schedules the work hardest shot first, assigns specialists and holds them to the shot specs. Use after treatment and shot specs exist and before anything is generated or rendered.

agents.name: qa-chief
agents.description: Runs the QA gate separately from production. Convenes a blind panel of three judges on an anchored rubric per deliverable type, takes the median, re-judges when scores spread more than one point, lets vetoes stand, and logs every score with the anchor it cites. Use at G8 for any deliverable before it goes to the owner.

agents.name: qa-rights-reviewer
agents.description: Independent QA and rights review. Must not be the agent that produced the work. Measures where measurable, names what was not verified, and may veto delivery on rights or technical failure.

agents.name: reference-forensics
agents.description: Examines real references (video, stills, sites, case studies) and returns measured DNA with keep / swap / never. Evidence over assertion; technique, not theft.

agents.name: script-writer
agents.description: Turns a picked idea into a hook bank and a timed script, screenplay or VO script shaped to the format (Shorts, long-form chapters), with a words-per-second budget and every factual claim flagged for the fact-checker. Use after a route or format is picked and before shots or voice are planned.

agents.name: strategy-chief
agents.description: Heads the Strategy department. Turns the intelligence dossier into positioning, the channel promise, pillars, series formats, a calendar, a monetization plan and 90-day goals, through three divergent strategy routes judged blind. Prepares the decision; the owner picks and locks.

agents.name: trend-scout
agents.description: Finds and verifies dated, measured trend and competitor evidence from public sources. Separates packaging signals from retention evidence. Never makes an untagged claim that a post went viral or outperformed; never spends credits without an approval row.

agents.name: voice-producer
agents.description: Produces the voice track: VO timing against the script, TTS voice selection or a human VO plan, pronunciation guide, pacing in words per minute, and loudness measured to platform targets. Flags every music and SFX licence to the owner. Use once the script is locked and before the edit.

agents.name: youtube-strategist
agents.description: Writes the algorithm-literate YouTube plan per channel and per video: long-form vs Shorts mix, packaging (title, thumbnail, first 30 s), Test & Compare, SEO, playlists, cadence, policy risks and the YPP path. Reads every platform fact from the knowledge file and re-verifies any older than 30 days.

skills.name: ai-film-treatment
skills.description: Write the treatment and the story, character and world bible for the route the owner picked, and the shot list that feeds shot specs. Use after the pick, before any shot spec or generation.

skills.name: brand-identity
skills.description: Procedure for a brand identity job in the harness (channel or studio brand: name lockup, logo, palette, DP, banner, kit). Agency structure with gates B0-B8, exactly 3 researched routes, mechanical checks and blind critics. Use for any logo, banner, DP, palette or brand-kit work.

skills.name: channel-dossier
skills.description: Build a Channel Dossier for any YouTube channel (and its Instagram if public) from one handle or URL - biography and timeline, formats and series, cadence, measured performance and outliers, packaging patterns, competitor map, monetization streams with earning points, risks and lessons to steal (structure, not assets). Use for "is channel ke baare me batao", "tell me about channel X", "competitors kaun hain", "ye kitna kamata hai", "how does X grow", or before planning a channel in the same niche.

skills.name: channel-launch
skills.description: Launch a new channel that has zero posts. Runs the 12-step Channel Launch workflow (brief, research, competitor evidence, positioning, pillars, formats, packaging, production system, 30-post calendar, measurement and review), with human locks and no invented data and no publishing. Use for a new YouTube, Instagram or other channel; orchestrates channel-strategy and content-programming.

skills.name: channel-strategy
skills.description: Research and position a zero-post channel. Category and audience research, competitor evidence from actual posts and videos, post-level deconstruction, an opportunity and positioning hypothesis, then the channel promise and editorial voice. Use for steps 2 to 6 of Channel Launch.

skills.name: competitor-watch
skills.description: Track and compare competitors or comparable studios and channels with dated, measured cards and honest limits. Use for a recurring watch or a one-off competitor study; paid data only with an approved quote.

skills.name: content-programming
skills.description: Turn a locked positioning into a programme: 3 to 5 distinct pillars, repeatable formats and series, a packaging system (title, hook, thumbnail or cover, caption, CTA), a production system, and the first 30-post calendar with a 90-day strategy. Use for steps 7 to 11 of Channel Launch.

skills.name: content-routes
skills.description: Produce three genuinely different routes (safe, brave, wild) with an axis table, blind scores and a contrarian pass, then present the best two for the owner's pick. Use after the research pack and before any treatment.

skills.name: operating-loop
skills.description: The Studio Harness operating loop for every job that produces a deliverable (channel plan, competitor or channel research, brand, banner, logo, thumbnail, script, reel, film, 3D video, post series, growth plan). Finds or opens the run, works only on the gate STATUS.md names, routes each task to its department owner and monitor, plans before building, verifies mechanically, shows only what the plan says, logs the owner's words. Use at the start of any job, when the session context says "Studio Harness is on", or when the owner says "agency ki tarah", "harness se karo", "plan banao", "isko poora karo".

skills.name: packaging
skills.description: Prepare titles, thumbnails, captions, platform requirements and a calendar draft as a social package for the owner to publish by hand. Never posts, schedules or messages.

skills.name: project-closeout
skills.description: Close a run. Writes the closeout record, sets the status honestly, and hands lesson candidates to the memory-curator. Promotion to shared memory is never part of closeout itself.

skills.name: qa-panel
skills.description: Score any deliverable the same way every time - three blind panel judges on an anchored rubric (rubrics/), median per criterion, re-judge when judges disagree, vetoes stand, and a calibration drift check before scores are trusted. Use at every QA gate before work reaches the owner, when the owner asks "kitne number milenge", "score karo", "kaunsa better hai", or when scores look inconsistent across days.

skills.name: qa
skills.description: Run independent QA and rights review on a run and write the qa-report with a PASS, FAIL or NOT RUN verdict. The reviewer must not be the agent that produced the work.

skills.name: research-pack
skills.description: Build a dated, evidence-led research pack with a validated source ledger and at least eight real references examined and measured. Use after the brief, before any route is written.

skills.name: shot-spec
skills.description: Write one complete, checkable specification per shot and move it through draft, approved_to_generate, generated and qa_passed. Use after the treatment and shot list; never generate before an approved paid_generation row exists.

skills.name: studio-brief
skills.description: Start a project. Declares the context, captures the brief in the owner's exact words, states business logic and success measure, creates the run folder from runs/_template, and lists the approvals needed up front. Use at the start of any new job.

tools.can: public YouTube/Instagram metadata, playlists, transcripts where available, video files for analysis; scripts/channel-pull.py + channel-stats.py turn it into measured channel data
frames, contact sheets, cuts, loudness (ebur128), encodes
deterministic 3D scenes via bpy, previews, renders
channel and video statistics, uploads list, comments (quota-limited)
YouTube Studio / Instagram Insights CSV exports or screenshots the owner provides
image, image-to-video, reference-to-video, text-to-video through whatever MCP connector or web tool the owner has; routing in policies/model-routing.yaml
voice-over generation or a human VO plan
compositing and timeline work via scripting (optional)
outliers, keyword research, competitor stats (account-bound; test before promising)
